correctness.rationale: For strictly positive a,b,c,d, the lifted history-state Markov chain is primitive with stationary pair law (u,1,1,v)/(u+v+2), u=(1−b)/a, v=c/(1−d). The strictly positive hitting recurrences for targets y=0,1 are solvable by one-step first-step equations; the eight solutions yield exact differences K00−K01=(a−b)²(1+c−d)/Δ and K11−K10=(c−d)²(1+a−b)/Δ with Δ=(1−b)(1−d)+ac+2a(1−d)>0. Thus four-history constancy forces a=b and c=d; in the converse the first-order random-target identity gives K=1+1/(a+1−c). The proof distinguishes positive return time from time-zero hits and four-history targets from one-symbol targets. Independently formed the four-state transition matrix and solved exact rational stationary and absorbing hitting linear systems in 21 sampled kernels; both squared gaps agreed. Only proof, not sample search, establishes all positive parameters.
